Wraps children with PageHeader + underline Tabs (route-driven) page.tsx <- REPLACE. {tabs.map(t => { const active = pathname === t.href; return ( {t.label} ); })}
{children} ); } ``` Use Link-based tabs (not shadcn Tabs) because each tab is a separate route. This is the cleaner pattern per settings.md. ### 2. `app/(dashboard)/settings/page.tsx` — **General** tab Server component. Replace the whole file. Sections as separate `` elements in `space-y-6`: **Section A — Workspace** - Card header: "Workspace" + description "How your workspace appears to clients" - Form fields (non-functional, plain static defaults — wrap in `"use client"` only if you need useState; or just leave as uncontrolled `defaultValue` — use uncontrolled to keep server comp; actually Card content with Input is fine as server component if the inputs are uncontrolled): - Workspace name: Input with `defaultValue="Acme Studio"` - Slug: Input with `defaultValue="acme-studio"` and small muted suffix ".clientloop.app" - Custom domain: Input with placeholder "portal.yourbrand.com", small helper text "Available on Growth and Scale plans" - Footer inside Card: right-aligned "Save changes" primary button (non-functional) **Section B — Branding** - Card header: "Branding" + description "Make the portal yours" - Row 1: Logo upload — small avatar-sized placeholder square (`size-16 rounded-lg border-2 border-dashed border-border flex items-center justify-center text-muted-foreground`) + "Upload logo" outline button next to it - Row 2: Brand color — a `size-10 rounded-md bg-primary ring-2 ring-border` swatch + hex input showing `#6D28D9` + "Reset" ghost button - Footer: "Save branding" button Because fields are uncontrolled, the whole General page can be a **server component**. No `"use client"` needed. Keep it simple. ### 3. `app/(dashboard)/settings/billing/page.tsx` — **Billing** tab Server component. Sections: **Section A — Current plan** (Card) - Large: "Growth plan" + "$79/mo" + "Billed monthly" - Right side: "Change plan" outline button + "Cancel subscription" ghost destructive - Plan limits grid (3 cols on md): "25 clients included · 18 used", "AI briefs: Unlimited", "Custom domain: ✓" - **Dossier wedge callout** — small muted text at bottom: "Unlimited seats on every plan" **Section B — Payment providers** (Card) - Header: "Payment providers" + description "Connect your payment accounts to bill clients directly" - Two rows (list-style): 1. Stripe — icon/logo placeholder (just `S` in a rounded square), label "Stripe", subtitle "Accept cards worldwide", right "Connect" outline button 2. Razorpay — same, label "Razorpay", subtitle "India and emerging markets", right "Connect" button with a small primary-tinted pill "Recommended for India/SEA" - Emphasize Razorpay slightly (matches dossier India wedge) **Section C — Invoices** (Card) - Simple table: Date | Amount | Status | Actions (Download) - 3 rows of mock invoices (hardcode inline for now): "Mar 10 2026 · $79.00 · Paid · Download", "Feb 10 2026", "Jan 10 2026" - Use shadcn Table primitives ### 4. `app/(dashboard)/settings/team/page.tsx` — **Team** tab Server component. Imports assignees from mock. **Section A — Team members** (Card) - Header: "Team members" + "{assignees.length} seats used" on right - Button in header: "Invite member" (primary, non-functional) - List (not table — list with dividers): - Each row: Avatar + (Name / role label) + right side plan badge + "Remove" ghost icon - Map over all 4 assignees **Section B — Seats policy callout** (Card with primary-tinted background `bg-primary/5 border-primary/20`) - Big headline: "Unlimited seats on all plans" - Subtitle: "Invite your whole team at no extra cost. We price by workspace, not per user." - Small "Compared to ManyRequests, SPP, and Copilot — all charge per seat." in muted text - This is the flat-pricing wedge surfacing in the UI. Make it visually distinct. ### 5. `app/(dashboard)/settings/notifications/page.tsx` — **Notifications** tab `"use client"` (for Switch state). Sections as cards: **Section A — Email notifications** (Card) - List of toggle rows: - "New request submitted" — on - "Request approaching SLA" — on - "Request delivered" — off - "Weekly digest" — on - Each row: label on left + small description underneath, `Switch` on right - Use `useState>` keyed by toggle id; Switch `checked` and `onCheckedChange` **Section B — In-app notifications** (Card) - "Comment on request" — on - "Mention in thread" — on - "Assignee changed" — off **Section C — Slack integration** (Card) - Not connected state: icon/label "Slack" + "Get real-time updates in your Slack channel" + "Connect Slack" button (non-functional) If shadcn Switch isn't installed, run: `cd ~/Clientloop && pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add switch`. All checks must pass. ### 7. Commit ``` git add -A && git commit -m "feat(settings): general, billing, team, notifications with underline tabs" ``` ## Hard rules - NO `any`, NO `@ts-ignore`, NO `as X` except `as const` - NO hardcoded hex except brand violet #6D28D9 in General → Branding swatch (it's a display value, not a style) - Use uncontrolled inputs where possible to keep components server-side - Notifications page is client-only because of Switch state - Layout uses Link-based tabs driven by `usePathname`, NOT shadcn `` - Each tab is a real Next.js route - Reuse `PageHeader`, existing Card/Button/Input/Switch primitives ## Report back (under 300 words) - Files created - tsc/lint/build - All 4 route HTTP codes - Commit hash - Any deviations

1	# Clientloop — Phase 1 UI Shell Plan
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	Clientloop is the codename (from Phase 18 dossier candidates) for the ManyRequests-style SaaS already researched across 22 phases in the Boldteq dossier (`ManyRequestsDossier.jsx`). The dossier returned a **conditional GO** with a hard gate at Phase 15: 300 waitlist + 10 paid LOIs before writing code.
6	
7	Yash is **intentionally overriding** the gate for a narrow purpose: build the **UI shell only** (mock data, no backend, no auth wiring) so it can be **used as the clickable validation asset** Phase 15 already requires (Figma-alternative prototype for LOI interviews). This is the cheapest path to satisfy the gate without wasting build effort later — the shell becomes real production code once the gate passes.
8	
9	**What we are building in Phase 1:**
10	- Agency-side UI shell for Clientloop
11	- Next.js 15 App Router + TypeScript (strict, no `any`) + Tailwind + shadcn/ui
12	- Three working screens: Dashboard Home, Request Inbox (table + Kanban toggle), Clients/Services/Settings
13	- All data mocked in `lib/mock/` — zero backend, zero auth, zero DB
14	- Fully responsive, dark-mode capable, production-quality look
15	- Deployable to Vercel as a static demo on day 1
16	
17	**What we are NOT building:**
18	- No Clerk, Neon, Prisma, Razorpay, Stripe, Claude API, tRPC
19	- No Request Detail + AI Brief screen (deferred — dossier's hero feature, but not in this pass per user selection)
20	- No client-facing portal (agency side only)
21	- No landing page / marketing site (separate Quill work later)
22	
23	**Why it matters:** the dossier's wedge is AI request-to-brief + flat pricing + Razorpay. The UI shell must *look* like a product that ships those things, even though none are wired. Visuals sell the LOIs.

Extracted from a 28-file zero-dependency visual upgrade on ConvertScan. 4 type: pattern 5 priority: high 6 last_updated: 2026-04-06 7 --- 8 9 ## When This Applies 10 11 Any project using shadcn/ui + Tailwind CSS that needs a visual refresh or modernization pass. These patterns require zero new dependencies -- they work purely with existing shadcn primitives, Tailwind utilities, and CSS custom properties. 12 13 --- 14 15 ### [PRIMARY PATTERN] --radius CSS Variable Is the Highest-Leverage Design Token 16 **Context:** Any shadcn/ui project where the UI looks dated or "boxy". The starting point for any visual refresh. 17 **Pattern:** Change `--radius` in `:root` CSS variables (typically in `index.css`). Example: `0.5rem` (8px) to `0.75rem` (12px). This single change propagates automatically to every Card, Button, Input, Dialog, Badge, Select, and other component in shadcn/ui because they all reference `var(--radius)` through the `rounded-*` utilities configured in `tailwind.config.ts`. 18 **Why:** shadcn/ui components use `rounded-lg`, `rounded-md`, etc., which are computed relative to `--radius` via the tailwind config. Changing it once ripples through every rounded element in the entire app. No other single change has this much visual impact per line of code changed. 19 **Example:** 20 ```css 21 :root { 22 /* Before (default shadcn) */ 23 --radius: 0.5rem; 24 25 /* After (modern, softer feel) */ 26 --radius: 0.75rem; 27 } 28 ``` 29 **Relationships:** Foundation for all other redesign patterns below. This is the single biggest typography win across all pages. The default shadcn page title style reads as "functional" rather than "premium". 39 **Why:** Modern SaaS (Linear, Vercel, Stripe) use larger, bolder page titles with tight tracking. They take less vertical space, feel lighter, and clearly indicate the active section with a colored bottom border. The default shadcn pill style is better suited for content tabs within a page section, not top-level page navigation. 229 **Relationships:** Use this for settings/config page-level tabs. Not for settings page navigation. 238 **Pattern:** Use a pill-style container with individual rounded triggers: 239 ```tsx 240 241 242 All Findings 243 244 245 Critical 246 247 248 ``` 249 **Why:** The soft muted container with white active pill feels modern and contained. The `shadow-sm` on the active tab creates subtle depth. This style works better than underlines for in-page content switching because it visually groups the tabs as a single control (like a segmented button). 250 **Relationships:** Use this for content-area tabs. Replace `opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100` with always-visible `text-muted-foreground hover:text-primary` or `variant="ghost" size="sm"`. 260 **Why:** The hidden-on-hover pattern hurts discoverability -- users don't know actions are available until they hover. Always-visible subtle buttons (muted color, small size) don't add visual noise but are always discoverable. 261 **Relationships:** Contradicts the common "clean table" instinct to hide actions. Related: `design/patterns/data-tables.md` action column patterns. 262 **Source:** ConvertScan (CROBOT), 2026-04-06 263 **Usage Metric:** 1 264 **Knowledge Version:** v1 265 266 --- 267 268 ### 5-Phase Redesign Execution Order 269 **Context:** Planning a visual modernization for any shadcn/ui project.
